Learn the source sequence in [shared Xmon inputs](tutorial-xmon-input.qmd) and
[source observations](course/source-observations.qmd). The
[SGB geometry concept](concepts/geometry.qmd#source-stage) explains the source,
planning and construction stages; this page owns their exact contract.

The in-tree `scgsim.geometry` API is SCGSim's current source-geometry
authority. It consumes structured PDK and component semantics and must not
reconstruct geometry meaning from solver-generated labels.

`scgsim.geometry` is the source-facing facade: `GeometryPlan`, detached
snapshots, normalized input models, adapters, stack/vacuum/curve preparation,
and summaries. `scgsim.geometry.compiler` owns the advanced route builder,
derived construction records, stage validators, and dispatch. The source
validator is defined in `scgsim.geometry.source.validation` and re-exported by
the compiler facade. Direct defining modules and model aliases are listed in
the [API migration reference](api-migration.qmd#geometry-and-compiler-api).

`build_component_stack()` composes two explicit authorities. PDK
`LayerStack` records supply materials, process layers, Z/thickness,
conductor/solution roles, and exact host volumes. Component annotations supply
local entity identity, ports, functional conductor regions, and topology
selectors. The Notebook composes named occurrences and assigns the final net
map; it does not author PDK or component facts manually.

In the public Xmon composition, the reusable child keeps its local pad,
coupler, mask, and a ground-arm metal contribution. That arm overlaps the
residual ground plane, so it is not a separate conductor Entity; modeling it
as one would duplicate metal. The root composition supplies one D0 and one D1
plane through the existing stack recipe, then unions the occurrence-local arm
geometry into the D1 plane using an explicit physical conductor-layer
binding; the draw or mask layer does not imply that target. It does not copy
full ground-plane Entities into each child occurrence or create planes
automatically. The Notebook owns the final `Net -> Entity` map across the
common planes, local device Entities, and named ground connections. Geometry
does not infer electrical connectivity or merge child net maps.

## Shared physical source and representation {#physical-representation}

The shared physical-source/profile scope is **CONVERGING**. Its
[physical representation contract](specs/physical-representation.qmd) separates
source physical classification from selected solver representation. One neutral
plan binds each original Entity and physical layer to its effective geometry,
support and complete enclosure trace. A body retains its actual source
endpoints and holes; a nominal layer span is not a replacement body. Missing
qualified contact or host incidence remains absent rather than inferred.

Palace and AEDT consume the same chosen interpretation. Different explicit
profiles retain their different approximation meanings; source attachment
normals do not decide native HFSS field-side selection. Historical recorded
source and runtime cohorts retain their original interpretation and identity.

## Source curves and native shared topology {#source-curves}

The curve scope is **ACCEPTED**. Polygon-only inputs retain their polygon
boundaries. Curves are explicit source declarations, not smoothing inferred
from a rendered layout or a mesh.

`SourceCurveSpec` describes XY coordinates in micrometres. Supported kinds are
`line_segment` (two endpoints), `circular_arc` (start, on-arc, end),
`interpolation_spline` (native interpolation through the supplied points), and
`bspline` (control points with explicit degree, rational weights, distinct knots
and their multiplicities when supplied). An optional `parameter_interval`
trims the native source curve; it does not rescale or refit its geometry.
Control points are not topological vertices. A `circular_arc` lowers to one
exact composite rational B-spline on native domain `[0, 1]`; its internal knots
separate the exact spans, and a trim may cross those knots. For a caller-authored
`bspline`, the supplied degree, weights, knots, multiplicities, and native
parameter domain remain authoritative.

A `BoundaryCurveChainSpec` binds an ordered closed boundary to `entity_id`,
`boundary_id`, and `selector_point_um`. The selector lies in the selected
Entity-owned **positive conductor region**. Compound source polygons are
unioned into logical polygons before selection, including bridge-encoded GDS
holes. `role="outer"` selects its exterior; `role="hole", hole_index=0`
selects the first recorded hole of that same polygon. A hole selector still
lies in the conductor, rather than in the empty hole. Hole order and source
orientation travel with the occurrence; native tags do not identify Entities,
Nets or source boundaries.

Component-semantics `boundary_curves` and `boundary_reconstruction` records
use local Entity and boundary IDs. GeometryPlan qualifies them with the
registered occurrence and applies its rigid XY transform once. For assembled
inputs, use `plan.set_boundary_curves(records)` or
`plan.set_boundary_reconstruction(records)` with qualified IDs. The detached
snapshot retains source polygons, declarations and occurrence provenance;
there is no live Gmsh model in the source snapshot.

`GdsBoundaryReconstructionSpec` requires explicit ordered `segment_indices`:
index `i` denotes the original edge from vertex `i` to `(i + 1) % N`.
The selected consecutive chain can cross index zero. `closed=True` selects
an entire ring; a partial chain keeps its original endpoints and leaves every
unselected straight segment unchanged. `anchor_indices` identify original
vertices used by the reconstruction, and `degree` and `parameter_interval`
retain the requested spline operation. A closed circular reconstruction uses
three explicit anchors; an open arc uses start, on-arc and end anchors.
Overlapping replacement chains or competing whole-boundary declarations
cannot own the same source segments.

For active declarations, the in-tree compiler builds one native OCC planar
arrangement before assigning material interfaces. Native Boolean history
retains source membership and trimmed parameter intervals. The same arranged
curves bound metal, dielectric and vacuum complements and port partitions.
The authored stack supplies Z; a collective native 1D-to-2D sweep of the shared arranged edges
creates exact ruled walls and preserves trimmed curve geometry. It retains
shared upper edges and one vertical edge per source vertex. Surface-first shells then form solution
volumes, including inner PEC void shells. Native construction errors propagate;
there is no straight-edge fallback, per-surface refit or global volume repair.

Stock Gmsh shell AutoFix can replace native face tags while correcting shell
orientation. SGB binds each repaired face back to its source `SurfaceID` by
complete native wire/edge correspondence, then carries that source mapping
through export and backend construction. Source identity remains fixed while
numeric Gmsh tags may change; tags, coordinates, area, and ordering are not
used to guess replacements. In the observed Circle PEC Shell construction, shared
faces and metal-cutout boundaries remained source-bound, while port sheets
stayed separately represented. If correspondence or required topology cannot be
preserved, native construction fails instead of emitting a fallback geometry.

Hidden same-Net contacts retain typed `MMContactRecord` ownership and never
become MM physical groups. Its additive `geometry_ref` contains detached
canonical point, curve and surface-loop definitions, with resolvable
`outer_loop_ref` and `hole_loop_refs`. Shared live boundary curves use the same
canonical IDs. Genuine polygon contacts retain `outer_loop`; genuinely curved
contacts record it as `None`. A planar contact can record its plane normal;
a curved wall records `normal=None` and its actual surface geometry instead
of a fictitious constant direction. Actual contact geometry does not assign
Nets, and different-Net contact remains a physical short error.

The construction plan's `metadata.curved_arrangement` distinguishes requested
source bindings/reconstruction from actual native intervals, memberships and
Z sweep. Its detached boundary transport retains the shared native faces and
edges; solver/mesh tags remain lowering evidence. Geometry order and finite
element order are separate choices. Curved model geometry does not make a
positive surface inset an exact curved-perimeter distance; see the
[EPR interpretation](eigenmode-epr.qmd#surface-identity-masks-and-loss-assumptions).

Palace Thin-Film and PEC Shell consume active curve intent through their
existing geometry entry paths. The existing route dispatch rejects active
curve intent on Retained Solid; polygon-only Retained Solid behavior is
unchanged.
AEDT's current planar lowering explicitly rejects active declarations; it does
not silently substitute the diagnostic polygon witness.

## Component-to-backend geometry contract

The accepted contract makes local component geometry and hierarchy explicit
before Palace or AEDT preparation. The public `scgsim.geometry.GeometryPlan` is the
mutable Notebook builder: it inventories expanded component entities and
stores the final `Net -> Entity` assignment. Its `prepare()` method returns an
immutable `GeometryPlanSnapshot`; `GeometryBuildInput` remains the normalized
geometry boundary consumed by the backend preparation paths.

Create the plan with `GeometryPlan(component=assembled, root_id="chip",
layer_stack=..., material_records=..., coupon_padding_um=...,
grid_size_um=layoutgrid_um)`. Set the source layout DBU to the selected
`layoutgrid_um` before constructing cells. Register each named reference
occurrence in parent-first order with `register_instance("chip/q0", q0_ref)`.
`plan.entities` exposes the existing semantic entity inventory with
slash-qualified `.semantic_id` values. The Notebook supplies the final map with
`set_nets({NetID: tuple(qualified_entity_ids)})`; `prepare()` returns a frozen
`GeometryPlanSnapshot` containing the normalized `geometry_input`, stack, GDS
bytes and digest, and detached source-occurrence records. It retains no live
component references. Palace and AEDT consume that exact snapshot through
`EigenmodeSim.set_plan(snapshot)`.

`GeometryPlan`, `build_gds_stack_geometry_input(...)`, and
`build_gdsfactory_geometry_input(...)` accept `grid_size_um=None`. With `None`,
the actual emitted `source_dbu_um` supplies the shared layout grid; an explicit
mismatch raises an error naming `grid_size_um` and `source_dbu_um`. SCGSim
checks the source DBU and does not mutate shared PDK or global state.
`metadata.geometry_grid` records `schema_version` with value
`scgsim.geometry.grid.v1`, the selected `grid_size_um`, and `coordinate_frame`
with value `assembly_xy`. It identifies the shared fixed-precision grid for
assembly XY/layer arrangement. Saved inputs without `metadata.geometry_grid`
retain historical interpretation. Original source identity is retained alongside the
computational change ledger, and walls inherit their snapped layout endpoints.
Z coordinates, film thickness, mesh, quadrature, and solver tolerances remain
separate; the XY grid does not assert that every 3D coordinate lies on it.
The fixed-grid XY boundaries form one shared noded network. Each original
directed ring edge carries its operand, ring and segment order through
explicit grid-pixel incidence; coincident edges retain every source. Raw
intersection and native-grid near-vertex events split these directed paths
before rounding.

Directed edge transitions determine face membership, and each operand is reconstructed
from those same cells without another grid snap. Ambiguous source paths or
inconsistent labels fail explicitly. Physical contact, hole and component
checks still compare against the original inputs.

For component-semantics schema v2, the paired stack adds derived source
occurrence records, not a new user polygon-selection API. Each
`metadata.source_occurrences` row binds a registered path and parent path to a
cell name, composed transform, and `reference_index`: the zero-based reference
ordinal in that parent, or `null` for the root. One registered occurrence names
one actual GDS reference. Consumers must first expand arrays into explicit
individual references; `GeometryPlan` does not auto-expand arrays. Each layer's
`geometry.source_occurrence_polygons_um` and each
`metadata.port_sheet_source_layers` entry's `source_occurrence_polygon_um`
preserve selected exterior and hole loops in micrometres. The reader checks
the paired GDS hash, binds each path to its recorded parent reference and child
cell, converts the source database units, reapplies the composed transform,
and recomputes those loops. This keeps touching same-layer geometry from
separate named occurrences distinct. Existing schema-v1 stack readers keep
their selector decoding behavior.

Component-semantics v2 also accepts
`component_semantics.ground_plane_contributions`. Each record has exactly
`local_id`, `plane_id`, `level`, `layer`, and `selector_point_um`. The local ID
names a component-local metal contribution; `plane_id` names a root-local
derived plane. `level` is the physical conductor level and must match the
target plane's `metadata.logical_layer_id`; `layer` is the source GDS
layer/datatype pair used with the local selector point. Thus a draw or mask
layer does not implicitly choose the target conductor face.

Preparation uses the selector to resolve one connected occurrence-local metal
region on the declared source GDS layer. That region can contain multiple
fused raw GDS polygons. The root-plane and occurrence paths use the same local
plane/mask/include geometry recipe. GeometryPlan applies the occurrence
transform once, verifies the resulting exterior and hole loops against the
paired GDS, and records them in the root plane's
`geometry.source_occurrence_includes`. The root plane's
`metadata.ground_plane_contribution_sources` retains the occurrence path, local
ID, physical level, and source layer. A selected region that contains a
separately declared local conductor on the same physical level is rejected.
These includes become part of the residual plane before polygon lowering; they
are not separate conductor Entities or Net assignments, and GeometryPlan does
not infer connectivity or promise separate measurements.

The plan owns the shared outer vacuum envelope. Set it before `prepare()` with
`plan.set_vacuum_region(padding=...)`, using the existing scalar, X/Y/Z tuple,
or six-face micrometre mapping forms. Both backends receive that same envelope;
once a `Sim` consumes a plan snapshot, attempts to add standalone
`set_geometry()` or `set_stack()` input, or a conflicting Palace
`set_vacuum_region()` / `set_airbox()` value, fail atomically. They cannot
replace only part of the bound source. To change the component, stack, or
boundary, update the plan and prepare a new snapshot, then call `set_plan()`
with it. A legacy standalone-input workflow uses a fresh `Sim`. No default
padding is inferred. Authored `D0_TO_D1_GAP` remains a separate vacuum entity
inside the outer region.

Component annotation schema v2 keeps conductor-region identity, level, layer,
and topology selector local to the component; it removes component-level net
and group assignments. Optional port records identify the local source layer
and target logical layer. Plan preparation verifies each source port and its
sheet and transforms the sheet once. Qualified lineage then identifies, for
example, `chip/q0/o_junction_lumped`. Palace binds that qualified port name to
its target logical layer; an AEDT junction uses the same normalized source
sheet and its recorded overlaps.

### Explicit rectangular junctions

Use `JunctionTerminalBinding` and `RectangularJunctionSpec` from
`scgsim.geometry` when a source port sheet represents a rectangular junction.
First prepare the plan to inspect its exact port-sheet, source-polygon,
occurrence, conductor-Entity, and Net identities. Bind the selected sheet and
both terminal owners explicitly, then call
`GeometryPlan.set_rectangular_junctions(specs)` before the next `prepare()`.
For a normalized `GeometryBuildInput`, `with_rectangular_junctions(build_input,
specs)` returns the corresponding detached request.

`RectangularJunctionSpec` names `junction_id`, `port_sheet_id`,
`source_polygon_id`, and `source_occurrence_path`, plus `terminal_a` and
`terminal_b`. Each `JunctionTerminalBinding` names one `source_entity_id`, its
`source_occurrence_path`, and its `net_id`. The two terminal Entities and Nets
must be distinct and must match the source plan. This explicit binding selects
the actual source overlap for each terminal; the planner does not search other
occurrences or infer owners from proximity.

The shared geometry interpreter derives the complete central rectangle and
terminal-owned end metals once, from the source database units and existing
physical attachment, before planning contacts, interfaces, and construction
catalogues. Palace Thin-Film continues to apply its existing
host-interface, common-plane, and common-volume rules. Palace and AEDT consume
the same derived source partition; AEDT validates that request rather than
deriving another rectangle. Palace `add_port(...)` still binds inductance to an
authored port name and does not choose the physical terminal owners.


| Fact or operation | Accepted contract |
|---|---|
| Component definition | Holds local polygons, source Entity IDs, ports, topology selectors, and local component facts. Reusing a component does not rewrite its local IDs. Schema v2 does not assign final Nets or expose a public `Group` API inside the component. |
| Component occurrence | `register_instance(path, reference)` binds a named path to the actual GDSFactory occurrence. Parent segments are registered before children. The path scopes entity and polygon identities before flattening; rotation and reflection apply consistently to geometry, selectors, and ports. |
| Notebook net mapping | Authors only the final `Net -> Entity` map on the `GeometryPlan`; components do not carry intermediate or child net assignments. Membership may be assigned once to one net; duplicate membership on the same net is deduplicated. There is no public component `Group` API, implicit connectivity, or child-net merge framework. |
| Assignment validation | Mapping updates are atomic. Unknown or ambiguous entity references and an entity assigned across different nets reject the whole update. An unmapped entity remains unassigned (`None`); a backend requires a net binding only where that backend operation needs one. |
| Source lineage | The immutable snapshot preserves source Entity and polygon identities separately from derived group membership. An Entity is lineage, not a promise of a raw per-Entity measurement or field expression. A `semantic_group_id` is not reused as Entity identity or source lineage. |
| Computational groups | New physical mesh grouping serves high-count geometry only. `StructuredFinalPhysicalGroupRecord` retains `conductor_component_id` when the group contains one conductor component; it adds sorted tuple `conductor_component_ids` and `conductor_component_ids_by_source`, mapping each source Surface ID to its scalar component ID. A new grouped record covers every eligible source member exactly once; all members require the same explicit Net, material and grouping criteria. Optional equipotential IDs must have the same value across the group; all-`None` is valid, while mixed `None`/present or conflicting values are rejected. Equipotential values do not supply a missing Net. The full source ledger remains available. Disconnected conductor islands may share one mesh group when those criteria match; each planned surface still has one component, and grouping does not imply physical contact. Palace aliases and EPR metadata preserve both new fields; repeated attributes for same-Net terminals and grounds are deduplicated. Records containing only the older singular field remain readable. AEDT owner/interface/integral groups remain backend-specific and keep their existing policy. |
| Backend lowering | Palace and AEDT consume the same prepared source snapshot through their existing preparation paths. Native aggregates retain their source members and coverage. This does not promise per-patch native results, per-Entity raw measurements, or per-Entity field expressions. |
| Vacuum geometry | Authored vacuum entities keep their names, materials, hosts, and per-domain analysis identity. At the source-input level, the plan adds one outer background domain as the semantic complement of modeled bodies and custom regions under the established SGB priority/cut rules. The backend owns how it represents that partition natively. The public `D0_TO_D1_GAP` remains a distinct vacuum entity. |
| AEDT object names | New native names are readable and deterministic, sanitized and disambiguated as needed, and remain bound to the original qualified Entity ID. Historical prepared names keep their version-specific reader policy. |
| Boundary defaults | Palace leaves an unspecified external vacuum boundary at its natural PMC condition. AEDT uses HFSS's default Perfect E. The shared input does not convert one policy into the other. |

These are the accepted V1 semantics. Source preparation establishes
the geometry input contract; it does not imply native geometry validation or
solver execution.

### Accepted Q3D source normalization

The Q3D GeometryPlan frontend is part of the accepted v2 implementation/API
(accepted 2026-10-09, candidate
`a932a173edb5c56ae14740ff5177190996255bdd`). Its recognized `airbridge_deck`
and `airbridge_post` records remain role-neutral source
geometry in the normalized snapshot; they are not given a Palace route
representation or a native conductor role by normalization. A selected Palace
route continues to reject conductors it cannot represent. AEDT Q3D consumes
the snapshot's final caller-authored Net membership and explicit physical
ground roles through its separate finite C/G source frontend. Source curve
intent is still rejected by current AEDT lowering rather than silently
linearized. This accepted source contract does not assert completion of a Q3D
solve or returned matrix observation.

## Current Surface-EPR direction {#current-surface-epr-direction}

The solve geometry route chooses how the physical metal is represented. The approximation profile is a separate choice: for example, `substrate_face` says where a thin film is represented, while Thin-Film says which solve geometry is used.

| Public name | Existing data code | Physical representation and scope |
|---|---|---|
| **Thin-Film** | `A` | Zero-thickness face-metal PEC sheets with finite bump/post PEC shells. Current Palace Surface-EPR direction. |
| **PEC Shell** | `B` | The closed exterior boundary of finite-thickness metal is PEC; Palace excludes the metal interior from its tetrahedral solve domain. Current Palace Surface-EPR direction. |
| **Retained Solid** | `C` | Retains the finite metal volume for advanced polygon CAD construction. This is not a complete Palace Surface-EPR route; active source curves and Palace ports are not supported on this route. |

The same `GeometryRoute` enum is re-exported from `scgsim.geometry`,
`scgsim.geometry.models`, and `scgsim.geometry.compiler`. An advanced compiler
call can import it from the compiler facade:

```python
from scgsim.geometry.compiler import GeometryRoute

route = GeometryRoute.THIN_FILM
```

The enum members are `THIN_FILM`, `PEC_SHELL`, and `RETAINED_SOLID`; their
stored values remain A, B, and C. The Palace-facing `representation` input
accepts `thin_film` and `pec_shell` as well as the legacy values `A` and `B`.
Retained Solid is a geometry compiler choice, not an available Palace
`representation` value. Existing serialized records and XAO naming keep the
legacy A/B/C codes so stored data remains readable.

The current Palace Surface-EPR direction includes Thin-Film and PEC Shell only. Existing pinned examples may still pass `representation="A"` or `representation="B"`; those are the legacy codes for the names above. They should retain the value required by their pinned package version.

## Historical SGB geometry distance bands (WITHDRAWN) {#surface-distance-bands}

SCGSim no longer exposes the SGB geometry-level distance-band producer. This section preserves the former design boundary for readers of older material; its `GeometryPlan.set_surface_distance_bands(...)`, `SurfaceDistanceBandSpec`, and Palace aggregation APIs are not current interfaces.

The withdrawn design partitioned an explicitly selected planar parent surface from its original exterior and hole edges, retained source lineage for each child, and passed those geometric regions into CAD and meshing. Its cumulative EPR aggregation depended on a completed Palace result and did not require Q2D. These historical regions were distinct from native Palace Mask/Inset rows: native Mask/Inset requests remain available through `inset_margins_um` when the selected Palace executable supports them. See the current [Palace Electrostatic contract](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#native-mask-inset) for that path.

## Internal semantic projection

SGB projects already-validated source facts once per source/model revision into
`scgsim.semantics`. The immutable projection is reused while planning a model;
it is not rebuilt by deep-copying a full stack for every interface pair.
Interface classification and each owner projection remain distinct operations:
solution solid/vacuum ordering is not interchangeable with declared surface
owners, legacy two-owner records, sheet owners, or aggregate physical-group
owners.

The projection can express finite PEC, surface-sheet MA/MS, local MM/MA patch
evidence, explicit side meaning, and outer/hole/seam provenance without
claiming that classification proves contact. Declared, planned, and observed
records remain distinguishable. Native tags and groups are opaque observations,
not reconstructed successes, and duplicate observations do not multiply one
semantic contribution.

`plan_route_surfaces()` owns the public projection boundary: it creates the
facade once when omitted, or verifies a supplied facade against the same route
and build-input fingerprint, then reuses it at the existing adjacency call
sites. Explicit authored interface kind and owner metadata take precedence
over derived defaults. Thin-Film sheet contact footprints remain an `MM`
topology relation but lower as the existing `MS` cap with its established
physical-name prefix; the surrounding sheet may still carry its independently
classified MA/MS evidence.

Thin-Film profile selection is optional for a direct semantic-core consumer.
Existing explicit Palace Thin-Film entry points still require
`substrate_face` or `metal_gap_equivalent`, and PEC Shell still rejects either
profile. With no core profile, coordinates remain unchanged and no collapse is
recorded. `metal_gap_equivalent` remains the existing effective coordinate
normalization; no reversible-collapse claim is made.

For a stack with no PDK vacuum layer, omitted conductor host declarations are
bound to the internally generated background only when the caller selects
`set_vacuum_region()`. The same normalized polygon-versus-substrate-region
contact check supplies Thin-Film physical support for both authored-host and
generated-background stacks. It considers complete exteriors and holes and
requires a unique positive-area contact; a bounding-box intersection,
point/edge touch, or auto-region edge is insufficient. An authored
but unresolved host name still fails instead of being silently rebound.
Single-substrate `substrate_face` has no opposing die or gap value; two
opposed substrates keep physical `substrate_face` and the distinct
two-face-only `metal_gap_equivalent` normalization. The generated Region is
profiled after the source geometry and partitioned around actual dielectric
and finite-PEC occupancy. Thin-Film sheets do not subtract a fictitious volume.

Thin-Film support is local rather than a whole-sheet label. The sheet polygon is
partitioned by exact bottom/top solution coverage before bare SA/AA surfaces
are constructed, so substrate holes remain holes and a partly supported stress
case retains separate supported and exposed children. Each child keeps ordered
bottom/top evidence; an MM contact cap retains only the side left after the
contact cut. Port footprints select the intersecting child and fail if they
cross incompatible local domain pairs. Fully freestanding sheets remain
unsupported.

The same local-domain partition is used when conductor faces are removed from
an SA patch. The planner subtracts only the face overlap with that exact
solution-pair patch, even when one conductor spans several adjacent domains.
After AEDT junction partitioning, only adapter-generated Thin-Film sheet
footprints are rebuilt from the final conductor polygons; caller-authored
interface declarations remain intact.

PEC Shell keeps finite geometry and records local top, bottom, and sidewall
material-side evidence. Geometry adjacency remains a set, whereas the additive
contribution ledger preserves semantic multiplicity. Two same-kind MA sides
on one Thin-Film child share one native surface and one aggregate Palace row;
they are not duplicated or multiplied. That aggregate requires Palace's
internal-boundary cracking and does not imply side-resolved numeric output.
The AEDT contribution catalogue is sourced from physically planned ledger
entries and groups one catalogue row by contribution identity while retaining
each distinct patch binding. A generic declaration without physical ledger
evidence remains semantic metadata and does not create an additional numeric
EPR contribution.

## Identity requirements

A handoff preserves:

- source SGB revision;
- semantic surface and volume identities;
- route choice and topology receipt;
- generated mesh/config identity;
- the mapping from solver entities back to semantic geometry.

External SGB revisions remain derivation history only. The in-tree
`scgsim.geometry` API is the current authority; its source-facing plan and
compiler stages remain separate. No direct external consumer or fallback path
is implied.

## Shared source facts for AEDT

`GeometryPlan` is the shared source frontend for Palace and AEDT. Its prepared
snapshot includes the normalized `GeometryBuildInput` polygons (including
hole loops), entities, solution regions, source provenance, and route profile,
along with the prepared stack and source-occurrence records. Source-linked
junction declarations retain their terminal nets, direction, dimensions,
inductance, and capacitance; those fields are not retroactively attributed to
the normalized `GeometryBuildInput`. AEDT does not consume
`ConstructionPlanRecord`, Gmsh surfaces, physical groups, or native tags.

AEDT preparation also builds a private, in-process representation context from
the explicit source/effective layer records. It binds each semantic entity's
physical-layer identity, source and effective Z intervals, and sheet/solid
representation, plus the already-mapped outer enclosure. The shared planar
contribution planner consumes those facts directly; it does not infer AEDT
modeling from entity metadata or treat the context as a Palace Thin-Film,
PEC Shell, or Retained Solid selection. The context does not alter the public plan snapshot, source GDS,
or serialized source schema. Palace compilation continues to use its explicit
Thin-Film / PEC Shell / Retained Solid contract.

An AEDT-owned binding sidecar must separately record each created body, sheet,
face, material side, selection, and saved-field expression against those
source identities. A native face overlap or adjacency query is observed
geometry evidence; it cannot manufacture source contact intent. Thin-Film
profile normalization still happens once at the shared frontend boundary, and
PEC Shell finite-body facts stay distinct from PEC approximation and the AEDT
implementation that realizes them.

## Preparation resources (CONVERGING) {#preparation-resources}

Use `scgsim.preparation.preparation_resources(max_workers=...)` around source
preparation and meshing to share one preparation worker budget. Without this
scope, preparation runs serially.

```python
from scgsim.preparation import preparation_resources

with preparation_resources(max_workers=30):
    snapshot = plan.prepare()
    sim.set_plan(snapshot)
    sim.set_mesh(threads=30, surface_threads=30)
    sim.mesh()
```

The scope reuses one pool for independent source recipes, indexed source-path
batches, zero-area support classification and per-operand reconstruction.
Results and task-local source audits merge in input order. Fixed-grid operands
share the same boundary network and labelled cells; source-path ownership and
face transitions remain deterministic. Unquantized parent planes keep their
separate construction path. Nested work reuses the budget rather than creating
another pool. Preparation tasks finish before the Gmsh child starts; its
requested thread limits must be positive and fit the explicit scope's budget.

This setting bounds SCGSim preparation workers; allocate the corresponding
CPUs through the scheduler separately. Gmsh thread limits and Palace MPI/OpenMP
settings control their own stages. `preparation_diagnostics(output_dir, profile=False)`
can record stage timings alongside this scope without selecting parallelism.

Each source-preparation call also reuses hierarchy extraction for the same
freshly read GDS cell and excluded-reference list. The cache ends with that
call.

Immutable raw polygons and pure subdivisions are also reused within a prepare,
adapter or compiler call when the complete ordered operands and grid context
match. Selectors,
source-record comparisons and physical/contact audits still execute on each
invocation.

Reconstructed grid-applied faces use one coordinate
representation per integer grid key, including their boundary-chain anchors;
raw source coordinates and non-grid local planes remain separate.

A topology
failure retains its original exception and adds counts, validity, area and
grid information without coordinates. Error-only witnesses distinguish the
initial grid realization, labelled cells and reconstructed faces from the
final shared-cell reconstruction. These witnesses do not replace the model or
its checks.

## Pre-solve input summary

`scgsim.geometry.summarize_geometry_input(build_input, *, prepared_stack)` returns an
`InputSummary` with detached `.data` and an HTML representation for notebook
display. Both Eigenmode facades expose `input_summary()` to combine this
normalized source with their configured backend settings. AEDT summarizes its
normalized build input and stack; Palace requires its bound `GeometryPlan`.
Passing a raw component without explicit normalization fails rather than
guessing a stack. The summary records source, entity, Net, material, Z/vacuum,
port, EPR, and run-control inputs; unset or unknown values stay explicit. It
does no file I/O, meshing, catalogue rebuild, or native solver inspection and
does not claim native geometry or run evidence.
For the source summary, `source.top_cell_name` uses a valid adapter-selected
`selected_cell_name` first, then falls back to legacy `top_cell_name` when the
selected name is unavailable, and otherwise is `None`. This display choice
does not mutate source metadata or reread the GDS.

Its notebook HTML presents source, backend, route, and count cards, followed by
Entity/occurrence/Net/material/source-Z, port/host/direction, junction A/B/L/C,
analysis-choice, film/loss/source/margin-assumption, and solver/resource
tables. The original detached JSON is in a collapsed disclosure. Unknown
values remain distinct from zero; `None` means all and an empty tuple means
none only for a selection, while an absent request is labeled not requested.
The HTML has no theme
argument and inherits the front-end light/dark palette; the detached `.data`
contract is unchanged.
